pageCache.text:
OUR PHILOSOPHY& VALUES
We are a school where every girl belongs, believes in herself and becomes the person she hopes to be, inspired to dream fiercely and move confidently into the world.
OUR PHILOSOPHY
At Francis Holland Sloane Square, our philosophy rests on three pillars that guide all that we do:
Belong: fostering a supportive and inclusive community where every girl feels valued and connected.
Believe: nurturing confidence, curiosity, and the courage to take on new challenges.
Become: empowering each girl to grow, thrive, and realise her full potential.
Underpinning these pillars is a commitment to excellence. Rooted in our values, they inform our decisions, our teaching, and our vision for the future.
Read ‘Our Philosophy and Values’ Booklet
OUR VALUES
In keeping with our Christian foundation, our values of love, courage, hope, humility, compassion and thankfulness shape every aspect of life at Francis Holland Sloane Square.
The three that guide us most intrinsically in all that we do are love, courage and hope.
Belonging is the lived expression of our value of love.
Believing is the lived expression of our value of courage.
Becoming is the lived expression of our value of hope.
Where next?

pageCache.text:
Harvest Festival Service at Holy Trinity Church, Sloane Street
On Friday 25th September, our entire pupil and staff body gathered in the stunning surrounds of Holy Trinity Church, Sloane Street, for our annual Harvest Festival Service.
Led by Revd van der Hart, the service encouraged us all to give thanks for our good fortune, to help those who are less fortunate and to practice our school values of love, hope and courage in all areas of our lives and relationships.
Highlights of the service included a reading from’ The Parable of Sower’ by Mrs Haydon, a talk on ‘The Farmer and the Field of Your Heart’, an introduction to Hammersmith & Fulham Foodbank by our Charity Ambassador, Bella, prayers led by our Deputy Head Girls, Chloe, Tally in the Upper Sixth and Sole, Margot and Carolina in Year 9, a beautiful performance of the late Brian Doerksen’s ‘Faithful One’ by our Senior Choir and Lower Chamber Choir and, of course, the opportunity to sing some of our favourite hymns!
Huge thanks to Revd van der Hart, to all our readers and performers and everybody who made the service so special, memorable and moving. We are also immensely grateful to everybody who donated so generously to our Harvest Festival collection. All donations will go to our charitable partner, Hammersmith & Fulham Foodbank, and will make an invaluable difference to the lives of vulnerable people in the local community.

COMMUNITY
It is our warm and welcoming community that everybody – visitors, pupils, staff, parents and alumni - mentions when describing what is so exceptional about our school.
The unstinting support, hard work and devotion of our Sloane Square Parents’ Association (SSPA) is a great signifier of the strength and spirit of this community, as is our strong relationships with our alumni, who regularly return to school to attend events and speak to pupils about their illustrious range of careers. Meanwhile, our outreach programmes, with charity representatives in every year group and strong partnerships with local charities, develop character and a sense of responsibility within the wider community.
Our students leave us to enrol in excellent university courses all over the world; yet they know they will always be part of the Francis Holland community. They are ready to enter the world beyond school with friendships and contacts that will last a lifetime and with the self-belief to become the leaders, thinkers and game-changers of tomorrow.

HEAD’S WELCOME
Since our establishment in 1881, Francis Holland Sloane Square has been a place where young women have discovered their strengths, developed their character, and stepped confidently into the world with purpose.
This is a school where every girl belongs, believes in herself and becomes the young woman she hopes to be: inspired to dream fiercely and to move confidently into the world with purpose.
Outstanding academic standards sit alongside exceptional pastoral care, with strong relationships at the heart of school life. Our values of love, courage and hope guide everything we do, shaping a community where girls are encouraged to think deeply, act with integrity and approach life with curiosity, creativity and compassion.
Through dynamic teaching, a rich co-curricular programme and a culture that values curiosity over perfection, we help our pupils develop the self-belief to take intellectual risks, explore their interests and embrace new opportunities.
Girls leave here as confident and thoughtful young women, ready to pursue their ambitions, lead with purpose and make a meaningful contribution to the world.
Alexandra Haydon Head

Welcome to a school where belonging and self-belief are at the heart of everything.
BE INSPIRED
We are an academically selective girls’ school where excellence is pursued with warmth, curiosity and joy.
For nearly 150 years, we have nurtured young women to think deeply, act courageously and step confidently into the world. Today, we are a vibrant, diverse community with intellectually rigorous and supportive classrooms that foster a love of learning.
Beyond academics, our rich co-curricular programme, including sport, creative and performing arts, entrepreneurship, leadership and service, develops independence, creativity, empathy and character.
Guided by our values of love, courage and hope, we are ambitious for what our girls achieve and for who they become: compassionate young women ready to shape their own future.
BE SURPRISED
Behind our door on Graham Terrace lies a site that seems far larger and more versatile than it appears, with a roof garden, netball court, gym, library, laboratories, drama studio and Sixth Form centre.
Every welcoming space has been designed to support learning, wellbeing and ambition.
We have exciting plans to unlock our site’s full potential, creating even more opportunities for ambitious young women who will take on the world.
Click here to view the development plans for our school site.
“My daughter feels known and understood; all the girls do, and that is why they flourish.”

READY TO FLOURISH?
Welcome to a Sixth Form defined by excellence, independence and opportunity. Ready to create your future?
SHAPE WHAT COMES NEXT
Sixth Form here does more than provide an exceptional academic and personal experience. It gives you confidence for life so that you feel empowered to move forward with ambition and purpose.
Think critically, act responsibly and develop the skills to thrive at university and beyond… it’s a mindset that has earned us national recognition as a 2023 Muddy Stilettos Special Sixth Form award winner and 2024 Muddy Stilettos Prepared for Life award finalist.
Small class sizes mean you will be known, supported and challenged. You will receive outstanding teaching with specialist subject support, plus a brilliant enrichment programme, leadership opportunities and all the guidance you need on higher education in the UK and abroad.
“Our daughter is leaving Francis Holland as a confident, resilient, strong woman who believes in herself. This is your gift to her. You did it with kindness and trusted that she would get there.“
Academic Life
ACADEMIC EXCELLENCE

pageCache.pageTitle: Outreach, Charity & Partnerships - Francis Holland | Sloane Square
pageCache.text:
OUTREACH, CHARITY& PARTNERSHIPS
Central to our mission as a school is the development of compassionate and community-minded young women. Our aim is for every pupil to be involved in outreach activities in every year of their time at the school.
A CULTURE OF SERVICE AND SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY
Our aim is to cultivate a lifelong appreciation of the transformative impact of charitable fundraising, volunteering and community action in every student.
We are proud of our longstanding tradition of supporting a wide range of charitable organisations through sustainable, high-impact fundraising. By building deep, mutually supportive partnerships over many years, we provide stability for our partner charities while offering meaningful opportunities for pupil involvement.
Charitable engagement enriches our educational provision: nurturing empathy and self-esteem, strengthening belonging and fostering global citizenship. Research consistently highlights the significant mental health benefits of service, with volunteering shown to strengthen wellbeing, purpose and connection. We see this reflected in our own community. Students develop essential life skills such as resilience, creativity and collaboration, all while discovering that generosity and joy go hand in hand. After all, we firmly believe you cannot spell fundraising without FUN.
LONGSTANDING PARTNERSHIPS, MEANINGFUL IMPACT
We are committed to building sustainable relationships of trust with our charitable partners. Our enduring partnerships with organisations such as Katherine Low Settlement and In-Deep span decades, in the case of Katherine Low Settlement, over a century. We also proudly support four students at Mvumi School in Tanzania, for whom we raised over £43,000 in our Clean Hands, Pure Hearts campaign in 2021, and work closely with Hammersmith & Fulham Foodbank, where we are one of the largest non-supermarket donors.
These sustained partnerships provide charities with reliable fundraising and dedicated volunteers. In return, our pupils gain access to bespoke educational experiences, from donation sorting visits to collaborative community projects.
By investing long-term rather than one-off support, we deepen our understanding of the needs of each charity and their service users. This approach ensures our fundraising is both impactful and responsive, creating benefits for our partners and transformative learning opportunities for our pupils.
PUPIL-LED OUTREACH AND VOLUNTEERING
All charity initiatives are pupil-led, encouraging enterprise, independence and collaboration. From bake sales to comedy nights, pupils organise creative fundraising events for local and international causes, as well as rapid-response campaigns during global crises.
Every Sixth Form student volunteers, whether supporting homework clubs and music therapy sessions, taking part in intergenerational activities at Eden Court Retirement Village, or contributing to co-curricular programmes at St Barnabas C of E Primary School and St Matthew’s Primary School. Outreach visits throughout the year, including foodbank warehouse donation sorting and seasonal community projects, further strengthen these connections.
Through these experiences, girls develop a practical understanding of the vital role charities play in society. Most importantly, they grow in compassion, confidence and conviction, recognising their responsibility to make a meaningful difference in the world around them.

THE HEART OF LONDON
Francis Holland is situated in a beautiful neighbourhood in the heart of London, just a two-minute walk from Sloane Square Underground and London’s iconic King’s Road.
CULTURAL CAPITAL
Nearby, green spaces such as Battersea Park are enjoyed frequently and offer a wealth of sporting opportunities. Just around the corner are the Royal Court Theatre and the Saatchi Gallery. From the Globe Theatre to the British Museum, the Imperial War Museum to the Courtauld Institute, Tate Modern to Tate Britain, the Houses of Parliament to the Old Bailey, hundreds of places of social or cultural interest are just a short walk or tube ride away, providing infinite opportunities to develop intellectual curiosity.
The school’s award-winning Futures programme is greatly enhanced by its central location, which facilitates frequent visits from alumnae and visiting professionals. In all year groups, pupils are encouraged to develop entrepreneurial skills through initiatives such as Young Enterprise, Tycoon In Schools and Girls Are Investors. In the Sixth Form, independent engagement with London life flourishes: lectures at Imperial and KCL are popular, while local sports studios such as KXU and Vita broaden PE beyond traditional sports.

STAFF & GOVERNORS
The schools are led by a Board of Governors, known as The Council, made up of 13 members who bring a wealth of experience and expertise to the non-executive leadership of the schools.
MRS ALEXANDRA HAYDON
Head of Francis Holland Sloane Square
Alexandra joined Francis Holland Sloane Square as Head in January 2024. Before joining FHS, Alexandra spent 5 years as Deputy Head Academic at Millfield, one of the UK’s leading boarding schools. Prior to that, she spent five years at St Mary’s Calne where she was Head of Science and Senior Teacher, and before that she worked in a variety of other schools, having begun her career at Graveney School in South London. In 2019 she won the i25 award for innovation and influence in the independent sector.
Alexandra read Biology at Durham University. She holds a PGCE and a Masters in Teaching and Learning from Oxford University, and her studies for a Doctorate in Education at Bath University are currently on pause so she can focus on Francis Holland Sloane Square. Alexandra is married with two teenage daughters and in her spare time enjoys reading, travelling and spending time with her family , recently completing (and winning!) a home spun Race Across the World challenge from Berlin to Istanbul.
Ms Clare Stansfield Senior Deputy Head – Teaching & Learning
Ms Clare Stansfield Senior Deputy Head – Teaching & Learning
Clare Stansfield studied History and Politics at Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, before completing a Master’s in History of Art at the Courtauld Institute of Art. She has taught History, Politics and History of Art, and has held roles including Head of Department, Oxbridge Lead and International Baccalaureate Coordinator. Since joining FHS as Head of Politics, Clare has taken on several senior responsibilities, including Director of Sixth Form, and was appointed to her current role in 2025. She also brings extensive experience in safeguarding and student wellbeing as a Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL).
Clare is committed to cultivating an ambitious, intellectually rigorous and supportive learning environment in which every student is known and able to flourish. Her work centres on compassionate leadership, inclusive pedagogy and the development of confident, critically engaged learners. Beyond school, she enjoys visiting art galleries and historic sites.
Mrs Sarah PittawaySenior Deputy Head Pastoral, Trust Safeguarding Lead
Mrs Sarah PittawaySenior Deputy Head Pastoral, Trust Safeguarding Lead
Sarah joined as Deputy Head Pastoral and Designated Safeguarding Lead in February 2022.
Previously Head of Secondary at an all-through maintained Church of England school, Sarah worked as a Senior Leader and Designated Safeguarding Lead in three large maintained London schools before joining Francis Holland.
Sarah holds a BA (Hons) in English from the University of Reading; a PGCE from King’s College London and has completed the National Professional Qualification for Headship. Sarah is Chair of Governors at an alternative provision school for pupils in need of support accessing mainstream education. Sarah is an ISI Associate Inspector and believes that excellent pastoral care is at the heart of a thriving school community.
Outside school, Sarah is a sometimes frazzled mother of 5 wonderful children/young adults while caring for 4 young cats and a lively labrador.
Mr Max DevenportDeputy Head Academic
Mr Max DevenportDeputy Head Academic
Max Devenport is Deputy Head Academic at Francis Holland School, Sloane Square, with strategic responsibility for curriculum, assessment (including external examinations), timetabling, reporting, academic standards and outcomes across Key Stages 3 to 5.
Max has held leadership roles internationally in Brazil and Malaysia as Head of Mathematics and previously spent six years as Director of Digital Learning at Latymer Upper School, where he led on whole-school digital strategy, remote learning during COVID-19 and articulated the school’s response to AI.
Max is passionate about creating dynamic curricula that challenge and inspire the modern student. When he can, he still loves being in the classroom and in particular enjoys championing mathematics as a subject for all.
Outside school, Max enjoys mountain climbing, trekking, art and puzzling.
Ms Jordana BerkDeputy Head (Co-Curricular & Operations)

Previously Deputy Head Academic at Old Palace of John Whitgift School, she led wholeschool academic improvement, strengthened outcomes, and oversaw the quality of teaching and learning.
Before this, Jordana was Assistant Head Staff Development and worked as a Director of Drama for over twelve years across the state and independent sectors, most recently holding the role at Whitgift School.
Jordana holds an MA in Education and the National Professional Qualification in Senior Leadership. Originally from Chicago, she benefited from a Liberal Arts education and completed her BA at Beloit College, where she studied Theatre Direction, Russian Language, and History.
Jordana believes that co-curricular life is essential to educating the whole child—promoting academic success, wellbeing, and the development of the skills pupils need for their futures.
Outside school, Jordana enjoys reading and runs a local book club. She also loves travelling with her family.
Miss Stephanie LambCOO
Miss Stephanie LambCOO
Stephanie is a former Tax Partner at EY, with over 25 years of experience in the professional services sector. She is a qualified Chartered Accountant and Chartered Tax Advisor. Over the course of her 16-year tenure as Partner, Stephanie undertook a variety of senior leadership roles in parallel with her client service responsibilities, including serving as a member of EY’s Global Tax Executive, the body responsible for setting the strategic direction of the global tax practice.
Passionate about the transformative power of education to enable individuals to achieve their ambitions, Stephanie brings extensive expertise in leadership, communication, operational transformation, and delivery excellence. She is committed to applying this experience to ensure the continued sustainability and growth of the Francis Holland Schools Trust and, in so doing, supporting and enabling the next generation for success.
Mr Tom RobertsonDirector of Development
Mr Tom RobertsonDirector of Development
As Director of Development, Tom leads on fundraising and engagement strategies. Tom has over 15 years’ experience in the independent school sector, previously heading up development for the Alpha Plus Group, working with 12 independent schools and three sixth form colleges in the UK and overseas and before that at Bradfield College, Berkshire. Passionate about widening access to independent education, since joining the Trust in 2021 Tom has launched endowment campaigns for transformational bursaries at both Francis Holland Regent’s Park and Francis Holland Sloane Square. He also serves as a Governor of Elstree School in Berkshire. Outside work, Tom enjoys walking, travelling, and playing real tennis.

Mr Matt BritlandDirector of Technology
With over 20 years’ experience in education, Matt has worked across both the maintained and independent sectors. His journey in independent education began in 2010 at Kingston Grammar School, followed by roles at The Lady Eleanor Holles School in 2014 and Alleyn’s School in 2018. In 2023, he joined the Francis Holland Schools Trust, continuing his commitment to excellence in teaching and learning and the implementation of technology across all parts of school life. Matt is passionate about the transformative role of technology in education and its potential to empower all staff and students. Beyond the classroom, he has a keen interest in collecting trainers and vinyl records. Music is a significant part of Matt’s life and he enjoys mixing and producing music in his spare time, blending creativity with technical skill. His diverse interests reflect a lifelong love of learning, innovation, and culture.

Ben holds a BA in Management and Human Resources from the University of Hull and is a Chartered Member of the CIPD. He joined the FHS community in September 2023, and has 7 years’ experience in the education sector, prior to which he held roles in local government, travel leisure and tourism. His aim is to provide efficient and effective HR systems and processes to support our colleagues to achieve their very best. Ben enjoys travelling and was fortunate enough to be able to travel the world with work in one of his previous roles, theatre and dining out.

AWARDS & ISI REPORTS
The outstanding results of our ISI Inspection Report in October 2024, as well as extensive national award success over recent years, reflect the extraordinary individual and collective achievements of our pupils and staff.
REPORTS
We were inspected in October 2024 and Francis Holland Sloane Square met the standards in every area*.
It is particularly pleasing to see that the ISI inspectors recognised the positive and safe pupil environment that we have at FHS. Inspectors found that the school has ‘created a positive culture in which pupils feel safe and can thrive’. The report also highlights that:
‘Pupils’ self-awareness develops quickly, and they learn to show respect for each other and other cultures.’
‘Pupils feel heard and supported.’
‘The school offers a broad, engaging and forward-looking curriculum… focus on encouraging pupils’ intellectual curiosity and deep learning.’
Download the ISI Report
*Under the new Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) inspection framework, brought in in Summer 2023, schools no longer receive overall judgements such as ‘excellent’; instead, the inspectors report on whether a school meets expected ISI standards in five key areas.
AWARDS
As well as having been named Sunday Times Independent Secondary School of the Year 2023, Francis Holland Sloane Square has received significant, consistent national award recognition in recent years in areas including Pastoral Care and Wellbeing, Sixth Form and Futures, Outreach, STEM and Sport. This holistic success is built upon the belief that girls who feel truly known within a happy and supportive community are freed to achieve extraordinary things, learning to take risks and to be fearless in attitude and ambition.

pageCache.text:
RESULTS & DESTINATIONS
Each year, our pupils achieve excellent public exam results and progress to leading UK and international universities. These achievements are the result of a close and dynamic partnership between students and their teachers.
GCSE Results
The Class of 2026 achieved exceptional GCSE results, with 46% of all grades at the top grade 9 and 75% at grades 9–8. In total, 90% of grades were awarded 9–7. These results are a testament not only to the academic strength of this cohort but also to their commitment, perseverance, and the guidance of their teachers.
Each year we see exceptionally strong value-added performance at GCSE and A Level. Girls consistently achieve grades that are higher than those predicted by their baseline scores. At both GCSE and A Level, our public exam results are, on average, half a grade higher than the baseline predictions, consistently placing us amongst the leading independent school nationally by this measure and demonstrating the excellent quality of our teaching and learning.
Grade A* and A / 9-7
Pass rate A* - C /9-4
GCSE Results
A LEVEL RESULTS
Each year, we see wonderful A Level success at Francis Holland Sloane Square; a reflection of the ambition, hard work and resilience of our students.
Consistently excellent A Level grades are the result not only of our students’ hard work and dedication, but also of the meaningful and collaborative relationships they share with their teachers, who put an extraordinary amount of care, compassion and challenge into their work. Our students’ families also play a vital role in supporting them and us throughout their time with FHS.
Whilst we proudly publish our students’ public exam results, we must also take care not to lose sight of the individual under a mound of statistics. Our students leave us as resourceful, imaginative and brave young women who are ready to dream fiercely, go out into the world and to make their unique mark on it. Whether they go on to Oxbridge or Russell Group universities, to top European or US universities, to leading art and drama schools or degree apprenticeships, each and every one of our students leaves us to begin the next stage of their adventure, equipped with the academic and pastoral skills needed to tackle whatever life throws at them.
A Level Results
EXTENDED PROJECT QUALIFICATION
Our EPQ programme at FHS is exceptional, both in terms of results and the ambition and variety of the projects we see each year.
With 51% of all grades at A* and 83* at A*-A, 2026 saw our best ever EPQ results. This success is all the sweeter because the EPQ is a truly independent project that develops skills vital to their futures at university and the workplace.
Leavers' Destinations
The consistently excellent performance of our students is underpinned by an academic and pastoral programme that builds resilience and a growth mindset. As well as gaining places at the highest tariff universities in the UK, significant numbers of our students progress to art colleges, conservatoires and drama, film or fashion school, as well as to Oxbridge and international universities.
In 2025, 87% of students achieved their first UCAS choice, and 100% received their first or second choice. King’s College London, Durham and Edinburgh were our most popular destinations with seven students going to each and a further five to St Andrews. Two won offers from Oxbridge. 15 in total went to international universities. Usually between a quarter and a fifth of the year group take a gap year; we fully support post qualification applications and find that universities like them too.
We are so proud of our students for having the originality and creativity to study a wide variety of subjects. Their interests range from engineering and Formula 1 to film school and drama, via International Relations and Economics. The support they are offered in school means that they feel confident to investigate and apply for new subjects – and new countries. We love hearing back from them and seeing them in school as alumnae to support current students.

pageCache.text:
The New Dining Hall Opens Its Doors
Over the summer, an exciting transformation took place at the heart of Francis Holland, with the completion of our beautiful new Dining Hall.
Created as the first completed project of the Unlocking the Potential campaign, the new space has been designed to be much more than a place to eat. Light, welcoming and thoughtfully designed, it provides girls with a space to come together throughout the school day, whether sharing lunch with friends, connecting with different year groups, or simply taking a moment to recharge.
Particular attention has been given to comfort, wellbeing and acoustics, creating a calmer and more enjoyable environment for pupils and staff alike. The flexible design will also support a range of activities beyond mealtimes, including educational workshops, events and community gatherings.
This project was only made possible through the generosity of parents, alumnae and friends of the School, culminating in the spectacular Her Story Gala last June. We are immensely grateful to everyone who supported the campaign and helped bring this exciting new space to life for current and future Francis Holland girls. Thank you.
Hannah Bennett, Development Manager
